candidates.title: Senators’ bill would provide pay raises for FRA inspectors
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Two U.S. senators have introduced a bill calling for increased pay for federal railroad inspectors, saying the Federal Railroad Administration has struggled to recruit and retain inspectors. Sens. Gary Peters (D-Mich.) and Jim Justice (R-W.Va) are sponsoring S. 5450, which would increase the pay classification for FRA inspectors by one level. This would boost maximum salaries for the jobs by nearly $20,000. “The United States railway system is critical to the success of our entire economy,” Peters said in a press release. “Federal railroad inspectors play a vital role in maintaining that system by ensuring railroad tracks, equipment, and operating practices remain safe and secure. candidates.title: NTSB releases preliminary report on NS conductor injury during shoving move
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — A Norfolk Southern conductor suffered serious injuries when he fell from the tank car he was riding during a shoving move, the National Transportation Safety Board says in its preliminary report on a Sept. 8, 2026, incident at Conway Yard in Conway, Pa. The report issued today (Oct. 1, 2026) addresses the latest of a series of serious injuries and fatalities that have occurred during shoving moves. The NTSB last month called for an end to crew members riding cars during switching shove moves, citing 14 deaths in such situations since October 2020 [see “NTSB recommends end …,” Trains.com, Sept. 21, 2026]. The injury occurred while the train’s crew was making a westbound move shoving a 219-car train from the main line into the yard. The conductor, riding a tank car, called for the train to begin the shove move, but the engineer then stopped receiving instructions from the conductor and could not reach him on the radio. candidates.title: Reading & Northern nears deal for Luzerne County, Pa., rail lines
candidates.excerpt: WILKES-BARRE, Pa. — A deal is at hand to sell rail lines in Luzerne County, Pa., to the Reading & Northern Railroad following results of two board meetings this week. The R&N has offered $7 million for the lines currently owned by the Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority, and says it will spend another $3 million to upgrade the tracks to be able to handle excursion trains. The redevelopment agency accepted that offer on Tuesday, Sept. 29, and it was also accepted by the Luzerne County Council on Wednesday, Sept. 30, the Wilkes-Barre Citizens’ Voice reports. The redevelopment authority had initially accepted an $8.2 million offer from R.J. Corman Railroad Group, which currently operates 27 of the 60 miles of authority-owned trackage and right-of-way under a deal expiring Oct. 30. candidates.title: Judge rules that East Broad Top Foundation can buy Mount Union, Pa., property
candidates.excerpt: HUNTINGDON, Pa. — A Huntingdon County judge has ruled that the EBT Foundation can buy the East Broad Top Railroad’s Mount Union, Pa., dual-gauge yard and 4.7-mile stretch of main line. The segment was split from the rest of the railroad in 2013-2014, when the East Broad Top Preservation Association bought it from the Joseph Kovalchick family. That sale was the first step in what turned out to be a stillborn effort to restore the entire 33-mile narrow gauge line as a heritage railroad. The deal, approved by Judge Ray A. Ghaner, is subject to approval of the Pennsylvania attorney general’s office, as reported in a paywalled Altoona Mirror article. Ghaner ruled that a right of first refusal claimed by the Foundation was, in fact, valid and gave it two weeks in which to close the deal, which is worth $2 million. candidates.title: Rapido HO scale drop-bottom gondola review
candidates.excerpt: A Pressed Steel Car Co. drop-bottom gondola has been added to the Rapido Trains HO scale freight car lineup. The newly-tooled model, based on original CAD files designed by the Northern Pacific Railway Historical Association (NPRHA), features plastic and die-cast metal construction, 33″ metal wheelsets, and semi-scale metal couplers. The Rapido Trains model is based on Northern Pacific’s 50000 through 50499 series of drop-bottom gondolas built by Pressed Steel Car Co. Inc. in Pittsburgh, Pa., in 1940. The 500 cars were assigned to general service, hauling coal, ore, pulpwood, scrap metal, and sugar beets, among other commodities. From 1966 to 1968, some — but not all — of the cars from this series were reconditioned. As part of that process, the rehabbed gondolas were reassigned to the 58250 through 58749 series. candidates.title: DCSA expands Track & Trace standard to IoT and reefer containers
candidates.excerpt: The Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) has released Track & Trace 3.0.0, expanding its container visibility standard to include IoT and reefer events. The new version builds on Track & Trace 2.2.0, which covers shipment, transport and equipment events. With the update, the standard can also handle data generated by connected containers and refrigerated equipment. DCSA said the changes respond to growing demand for more consistent smart container data across the supply chain. New visibility for connected and reefer containers Track & Trace 3.0.0 introduces two new event types: IoT events and reefer events. IoT events include information such as container geolocation, geofence crossings and door status. Meanwhile, reefer events cover temperature readings, setpoint adjustments, power status and alarms. candidates.title: Maersk raises intermodal fuel fees in El Salvador and Guatemala
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will increase its Intermodal Fuel Fee for truck transportation into El Salvador and Guatemala amid higher global energy prices and rising landside operating costs. The revised Export Fuel Surcharge and Import Fuel Surcharge levels will apply from 29 September 2026 for non-FMC shipments and 29 October 2026 for FMC-regulated shipments, based on the price calculation date. The new levels will remain effective until further notice. The charges will appear on invoices under the EFS and IFS codes. Maersk attributed the increases to the impact of the Middle East security situation on global fuel availability and intermodal transport costs. The carrier said the adjustments aim to maintain service continuity and secure sufficient vendor capacity across its landside network.

candidates.title: Suez Transits Are Up 59%, and Rates Are About to Fall
candidates.excerpt: Suez Transits Are Up 59%, and Rates Are About to Fall Carriers Have Returned to Suez, and the Data Confirms It Maritime media sources state that container shipping is moving from a capacity shortage to a surplus as carriers return to Suez and shorter voyages free up ships. Windward MIOC data supports this claim. Suez containership transits rose 59% from March to September, from 139 to 221. The growth came from large ships, 300m and above, up to 24,000 TEU, the post-Panamax to ultra-large vessels used on main Asia-Europe services, which rose from 22 to 127 transits a month. At the start of the war in March, most of these were only calling at Red Sea ports, and by August, most were sailing to Asian markets. Europe-to-Asia transits grew faster than Asia-to-Europe. candidates.excerpt: Drewry’s Global Container Port Throughput Index fell 3.3% MoM in July The Drewry Container Port Throughput Indices are a series of calendar adjusted volume growth/decline indices based on monthly throughput data for a sample of over 340 ports worldwide, representing over 80% of global volumes. The base point for indices, January 2019 = 100. Drewry has developed a nowcasting model that uses vessel capacity and terminal duration data (derived from our proprietary AIS model) to make short-term predictions of port throughput. Drewry’s Global Container Port Throughput Index fell 3.3% MoM in July, down 1.3% YoY. The rolling 12-month average growth rate for global port handling fell to 3.8%, the lowest level recorded in over two years. Global throughput growth continues to slow, up only 2.2% YTD in July. candidates.excerpt: Apollo rolls out daily pricing across $850bn credit business Apollo Global Management has begun rolling out daily pricing across its $850bn (£643.7bn) credit business as the industry tries to build a more transparent private credit market. The $1tn alternatives giant launched daily pricing for investors in its investment-grade fixed income replacement products on 1 July, and said today (1 October) that it had extended this to a range of direct lending, asset-backed finance, multi-credit and opportunistic credit vehicles. Apollo chief executive Marc Rowan first set out the plan on the firm’s first-quarter earnings call in May, as private credit funds faced a surge in redemption requests from retail investors. Apollo said the move was intended to promote “greater transparency” as a wider pool of investors moves into private credit. candidates.title: Bathla collapse set to sharpen investor scrutiny of Australian private credit
candidates.excerpt: Bathla collapse set to sharpen investor scrutiny of Australian private credit Investors in Australian private credit are expected to ask much tougher questions of their managers after the collapse of property developer Bathla Group. The Sydney-based developer fell into administration on 25 August owing around A$3.4bn (£1.8bn) to investors, with about 40 private credit funds having exposure. While some within the industry suggest benefits might come from the challenges brought on by the company’s collapse, more pain likely awaits the industry before any of the positives are felt. This week, the Australian alternatives manager Metrics Credit Partners has suspended trading in three of its ASX-listed funds and frozen investor withdrawals from some of its vehicles. Centuria Bass paused redemptions and applications to two of its credit funds on 14 August, after a rise in redemption requests driven by concerns about Bathla. candidates.title: Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. The 25 crew of the vessel were reported to have abandoned ship into a lifeboat and were rescued by another MSC vessel MSC Ruby which answered the distress call. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east.
